questions.q: Which T-SQL feature is closest to checking df["order_id"].is_unique in pandas?
questions.explain: is_unique verifies that a key column has no repeated values, which is what a primary key or unique constraint enforces in the database.

questions.q: How do you check that every customer_id in orders exists in the customers table?
questions.explain: isin against the other table's key column is the pandas version of a foreign key check.

questions.q: What happens when a NaN value is passed through Series.between(0, 10000)?
options: It returns True, since NaN is not outside the range
It returns False for that value, so it fails the range check
questions.explain: A missing value is not between any two numbers, so between() yields False for it. That is why the lesson's function checks completeness separately.

questions.q: Why is it better to negate a check and filter (df[~check]) than to just print False?
options: It returns the actual offending rows you need to investigate or send to the data owner
questions.explain: A bare True/False says something is wrong; the filtered rows say what and where.

questions.q: What is the purpose of assert not failed, f"Validation failed: {failed}" at the end of a validation step?
options: To delete the failing rows from the DataFrame
To write the report to a CSV file
To stop the run with a clear message so bad data cannot flow downstream unnoticed
questions.explain: assert raises an AssertionError with your message when the condition is false, stopping the notebook or script at the point of failure.
